chunks: Say the ‘ishā’ (night) prayers with them when twilight disappears and upto one third of the night.

key_terms.الشَّفَقُ: Twilight, specifically the red glow in the sky after sunset

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended time range for performing the Ishaa prayer according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS) instructs governors to lead the congregation in ‘Ishā’ prayer from the disappearance of twilight until one-third of the night, emphasizing communal unity and the importance of timely worship. This ruling reflects the early Islamic practice of consolidating prayers to facilitate governance and community cohesion, a key theme in Nahj al-Balagha’s administrative letters. The timing aligns with the Shia understanding of ‘Ishā’ as having an extended preferred window, balancing devotion with practical considerations for the populace.
